reader.requirement: At --std 85 a RECORD DELIMITER IS STANDARD-1 clause may be written only for a file whose external medium is magnetic tape; an implementation that claims no reel device need not implement the phrase (a hardware-dependent element) but must document its absence.
reader.edition-search: Same path as SR1: FileControlBinder.BindFileControl captures STANDARD-1 into FileModel.RecordDelimiter and calls EditionContext.Declined(RecordDelimiterUnsupported); Declined reads only the descriptor severity and --permissive. Grepped for RecordDelimiter/STANDARD_1 in src (excluding Generated): no CobolVersion, ConstructRegistry or edition test on the path.
reader.witnesses-cover: part: pb292_record_delimiter_witness writes STANDARD-1 with and without IS on mass-storage (disk) files and pins the warning through DocumentedNonSupportWitnessTests; no tape medium exists to exercise the positive half

probes.printed: warning COBOL1778: '... STANDARD-1 is a processor-dependent element ... whose ... medium is a tape drive, and WiseOwl COBOL provides no reel device ... The clause is ACCEPTED and has no effect'; files FV and FF (disk files) compile and round-trip: '03 ABC 0123456789'
probes.expected: STANDARD-1 on a non-tape file: the phrase is the §1985:C.3 item 6 hardware-dependent element, not implemented and documented absent; flagged at compile time

probes.printed: warning COBOL1778 + error COBOL2912 for a RELATIVE file
probes.expected: STANDARD-1 on a relative (mass-storage) file entry is refused by the format

OK  §1985:I.1.5.2.5.1  (1.5.2.5.1 Hardware Dependent Language Elements)  the text is in the clause
OK  §1985:C.3  (3. <u>HARDWARE DEPENDENT LANGUAGE ELEMENT LIST</u>)  the text is in the clause

reader.notes: STANDARD-1 is a 1985 hardware-dependent element (§1985:C.3 item 6) and §1985:I.1.5.2.5.1 says such elements for unclaimed hardware need not be implemented, their absence specified; docs/conformance/2/26.md documents it Not claimed (no reel device) and COBOL1778 flags every use, so no tape-medium file can exist for SR2 to admit. The decline text cites the 2023 licence (§2023:4.2.6, Annex A.3 item 26) rather than the 1985 one; same behaviour at 2023.
